messages:
maria_support: FYI — ACME (enterprise) opened an urgent ask: 1) they need us to explicitly state whether Redwood is a data controller or processor for (a) API request payloads, (b) system/observer logs, and (c) KMS metadata; 2) confirm whether our subprocessor list includes our KMS/HSM partner and their EU residency; 3) they also saw an erasure call return 401 on their dedicated tenant. Repro below. Can security/legal/eng advise ASAP? @sam_security @lisa_legal @alek_engineer

maria_support: Repro (customer supplied):
```
POST /v1/erase HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-tenant-42
Content-Type: application/json

{"customer_id":"acme-123","request_id":"req-2026-03-15-01"}
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized (no body).

alek_engineer: thanks — can you drop the tenant id + request id and approximate time? I'll pull service logs and KMS call traces.

maria_support: tenant=acme-tenant-42, req=req-2026-03-15-01, ts=2026-03-15T10:12:03Z

deploy-bot: audit-export: log bundle ready for acme-tenant-42 -> https://internal/redwood/logs/export/2160003456 (expires in 7d) :lock:

julian_sre: quick log snippet from the bundle (truncated) ->
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z INFO auth: incoming erase request tenant=acme-tenant-42 req=req-2026-03-15-01 token_id=tok-9f2c
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z WARN kms: decrypt failed tenant=acme-tenant-42 key=cmk-acme-01 err=AccessDenied
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z ERROR erase: aborting req=req-2026-03-15-01 status=401
```

sam_security: short answer on roles: for customer request payloads (the data you send to /v1/* endpoints) Redwood acts as a processor — we process on behalf of the customer (controller). For our internal telemetry/aggregated product analytics we are controller for that telemetry.

sam_security: about KMS/HSM subprocessors: we engage a managed HSM provider (CloudHSM Inc.) for hardware crypto ops in some regions. Whether that provider is a "subprocessor" for GDPR depends on if customer-managed keys are provisioned through them. If the customer supplies their own CMK under their tenancy and controls the key material, we still call the HSM as a subprocessor for cryptographic operations. I'll confirm the exact EU location for CloudHSM Inc. (they have eu-west-1 / frankfurt endpoints).

lisa_legal: we can provide a DPA excerpt. proposed text for subprocessor clause (draft): "Subprocessors engaged for cryptographic operations may include CloudHSM Inc. (operating in EU regions). Customer-managed keys remain under the customer's control; Redwood acts as Processor for request payloads and will only access/decrypt data when instructed or to fulfill the request. Redwood will provide subprocessor list and locations on request and notify of changes per Section 4 (30 days)."

lisa_legal: if ACME needs signed wording including residency we can add a short addendum. pinging privacy-team if they want to add stricter residency guarantees.

alek_engineer: on the 401 + AccessDenied: looks like two things combined: (1) the incoming API key used was a tenant API key but missing the required tenant header (we require X-Redwood-Tenant for dedicated tenants in this flow), so request failed early; (2) KMS call failed because the CMK's key policy doesn't include our redwood-service principal, so HSM refused decrypt. Repro locally:
```
# reproducer (will return 401 if header missing)
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/erase \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-tenant-42" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-tenant-42" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"acme-123","request_id":"req-2026-03-15-01"}'
```

alek_engineer: recommended remediation for customer: 1) ensure their service principal/key is scoped correctly and include X-Redwood-Tenant on calls; 2) update the CMK key policy to allow redwood-service (we can provide the exact ARN/principal). If they want we can do a guided session to update policy.

julian_sre: confirmed from infra logs: KMS request id = kms-zz-3344 returned AccessDenied from CloudHSM endpoint eu-central-1. I pulled the key policy snapshot; it's missing redwood-service principal.

lisa_legal: action for DPA/contract: I'll draft the addendum and a short paragraph listing current cryptographic subprocessors + region. Expect draft by EOD (+1 business day).

sam_security: i'll follow up with CloudHSM ops to confirm EU locations and whether any sub-subprocessors are used.

maria_support: action items i) tell ACME to add X-Redwood-Tenant header and we can provide curl snippet; ii) offer guided policy update for their CMK or rotate to Redwood-managed keys if they prefer; iii) legal to send DPA excerpt + addendum. I'll reply to customer with ETA: technical fix now (hours), formal DPA text EOD/next business day. Ticket PRIV-2026-88 opened and assigned to privacy + infra.

maria_support: customer-facing reply (draft): "Thanks — we are a Processor for request payloads. For telemetry we are a Controller. Our HSM vendor (CloudHSM Inc.) operates in EU regions; legal will share formal DPA language and subprocessor list shortly. For your 401, please include X-Redwood-Tenant header and we can walk through CMK policy changes. Will follow up with timeline." :thumbsup:

alek_engineer: i'll coordinate a 30-min call with ACME SREs if they want.

maria_support: closing loop here — will post customer ack when they confirm.
